ACK 1f69c5cfdd9a21e03bedcb4edd14c4fb13954b7c

Reviewed the updated diff and had me clanker rerun GCC/Clang object comparisons at -O0 and -O2. The interpreter changes only assertion diagnostic line numbers, and preserving those gives byte-identical objects.

Also prefer hodlinator’s formatting in interpreter.cpp as the braces serve no scoping purpose and removing them makes the unconditional return clearer IMO.

lgtm. Should be fine for this codebase, as we already require "unreachable" code to be marked with an abort instead of UB.

Trivial change: applying the following whitespace-only patch gives byte-identical assembly with GCC/Clang - can't be simpler than this.

<details><summary>Patch</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/src/script/interpreter.cpp b/src/script/interpreter.cpp
--- a/src/script/interpreter.cpp
+++ b/src/script/interpreter.cpp
@@ -675,7 +675,11 @@
                 break;
 
                 case OP_RETURN:
+
                     return set_error(serror, SCRIPT_ERR_OP_RETURN);
+
+
+
 
                 //
                 // Stack ops
```
</details>

comments.body: It does appear that this is likely removable too.
Happy to do what reviewers prefer here.

OK I pointed Astra at this to try and get more guarantees around removal...

It compiled the interpreter translation unit before and after removing this `break`, using GCC 15.3.0 and Clang 19.1.7 at both `-O0` and `-O2` (as we use in Guix builds), with assertions enabled.

**All four pairs produced byte-identical object files when preserving the newline.** Deleting the whole line changed only assertion diagnostic line numbers.

[Clanker's full report](https://gist.github.com/willcl-ark/4643419ce01108779d587a7e7ecced35). 

This further supports removing the unreachable `break` IMO.
I might swap to that once rebased for #36783.
Now that I've taken the diff, I'm going to mark this as resolved, so review can restart in a clean thread.
